To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the shape of the person in an image can be evaded by manipulating the input image in a way that is imperceptible to a human; and (2) this is possible by applying adversarial perturbances to the image in the spatial domain, which can be applied by an attacker without any knowledge about the internal workings of the model.
we show that shape estimation can be manipulated in a privacy preserving manner.
1. Shape evasive perturbations are more effective when applied in a multi-stage approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: Can we prevent body shape inference by adversarial perturbements in the first place?

the following questions: How can we manipulate images such that they are not recognized as a person anymore? Can we manipulate the shape estimation of state of the art approaches? How can we manipulate the shape of a person without affecting the appearance? Can we manipulate images such as to make the shape estimation fail?
the question if the privacy risks associated with the new generation of body shape estimation methods can be effectively mitigated
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
shape evasion is a challenging problem that can only be solved with a combination of multiple strategies and is highly dependent on the specific model and dataset.
the current shape inference approaches are still far away from being robust against such attacks.
while the shape estimation of single stage approaches can be easily evaded by adding small perturbations, multi stage approaches are much more robust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
shape evasion is a hard problem and that the most effective strategy is to use a generative adversarial network that learns to generate realistic images that are not associated with the target shape.
the shape estimation is not only sensitive to the image content but also to the overall pose.
the more stages a model has the more effective the manipulation can be, but the more complex and expensive the manipulation becomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adversarial perturbements can be successfully used for shape evasion in the first two stages of the pipeline.
shape inference can be successfully evaded in the presence of adversarial attacks.
a multi stage architecture is more susceptible to adversarial attacks and can be manipulated to evade shape estimation with high success rates.
